b: The next day the shoes still hadn't dried much… The smell of a dead rat began to peep out gently… We used the dryer a bit more… I gave up, tied my shoes up and decided to deal with them in Colombo

Now they set off to see a waterfall.. All this climbing up and down mountains is a bit of a struggle for me.. Since I have wheezing, I get breathless more than most.. If I took my medicine properly and exercised, it would be enough.. But since we're the caste that only preaches to others, I suffer

So, why make trouble in a place I'd come to visit, I thought, and didn't go.. These guys talked about renting bikes and took two.. They didn't even ask for a licence.. just gave them.. So while they went on the bikes, I walked around the town alone (without getting lost)

As I went, some women in traditional dress, seeing I was a foreigner, called me to come to their village… Since Mithra had told me the day before, I understood.. There are lots of traditional villages here… Their economy depends on tourism, like walking through the villages, staying in a hut with them, and so on.. If I hadn't known this, I'd have thought it was some kind of trap.. Though I tactfully managed by saying I'd come later, they only let me go after making me promise.. Glad to get away, I came back to the room

It was just right for them to come back after seeing the waterfall and all… They'd somehow got used to riding motorbikes on the other side of the road… They said you have to pay to see the waterfall too…but it's very beautiful apparently… For the rest of the story you'll have to ask them

After that we had to see Cat Cat village, and they took us there on the bikes by turns.. That's a village too… You can take photos.. You can buy lots of things… A place in harmony with a tourism economy based on hill-village life…Now, walking through it, our Mithra got the urge to put on that traditional dress and take a photo.. Though we said it was a waste of money, she didn't give up. She put on a dress like a street magician's and had her photo taken

Lots of walking, terribly tired .. Mithra's foot swelled up a bit more and started to hurt too … We somehow put her on a bike and sent her to the room and followed behind…But all her ailments vanished the moment she saw a salon.. She paid there and came back having only had her hair washed.. For that money you could bathe with shampoo for four years…It wasn't just me who didn't understand this; the boys with me didn't either.. Mithra scolded us, saying we'd never understand

From there we went to the stand to take the bus.. At first I was down for a separate bus.. While I was scared of what problem would come up here, in the end the office said it was the same bus for everyone… That was a bit of a relief..But instead of an ordinary bus, something called a love bus came.. Apparently two people can travel in one cabin… Just as I was thinking I could buy a house in Vietnam, they said only one person per cabin… It was a letdown…
Travelling like this, by dawn we were back in Hanoi again
note: "Cat village" is a joke on the name of Cat Cat village near Sapa.
